Marissa / team —

Happy to take point on this. Summary and artifacts below. I can join a technical call; available next week Tue/Thu mornings PT.

Pen test:
- We engaged an external testing firm in 2026-11; the full report is classified (contains internal hostnames/IPs and PoC details).
- We can produce a redacted vendor-ready PDF that strips PoCs, internal network identifiers, and any customer data.
- Attachment: Redwood_PenTest_Summary_202611.pdf (redacted summary we typically share) — I can create a further redacted version if FinHealth needs it.

Vulnerability management (summary):
- Scanning cadence: external pen tests annually (third-party), internal dynamic scans weekly, authenticated scans & SAST monthly, dependency scanning on every build.
- SLA / remediation targets by severity (initial triage & fix target):
   * Critical: acknowledge within 4 hours, mitigation/patch within 72 hours or hotfix deployment.
   * High: acknowledge within 24 hours, remediation within 30 days.
   * Medium: remediation within 90 days (or earlier via patch cycle).
   * Low: tracked to next scheduled release.
- Disclosure: coordinated disclosure with reporters; standard 90-day disclosure window for public reports after a patch is available. We notify affected customers for any incident in accordance with our incident response plan.

Evidence & links:
- SOC 2 Type II (2026) report is available under secure drive: https://drive.redwood.com/secure/reports/SOC2-2026-Redwood
- I will attach the pen-test summary and our vulnerability management process doc.

Attachments: [Redwood_PenTest_Summary_202611.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB)], [Redwood_Vuln_Management_Process.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

Let me know if FinHealth requires additional detail or an NDA for more sensitive artifacts.

—Rishi
